issues.issue: Is a conditional sentence a term of imprisonment under s. 36(1)(a) of the IRPA?
issues.applicant_position: A conditional sentence is not a term of imprisonment under s. 36(1)(a), so Tran was not inadmissible on that ground.
issues.respondent_position: Minister says a conditional sentence counts as a term of imprisonment, relying on rejected amendments to exclude it.
issues.result_quote: the phrase “term of imprisonment” in s. 36(1) (a) of the IRPA cannot, by either standard of review, be understood to include conditional sentences.

issues.issue: Is the maximum punishable term assessed at the time the offence was committed, or at sentencing or admissibility?
issues.applicant_position: The maximum is fixed at the time of the offence; Tran could not have known of the later increase.
issues.respondent_position: The maximum is measured when admissibility is assessed, under the law in force then, reflecting current views of seriousness.
issues.result_quote: refers to the maximum sentence that the accused person could have received at the time of the commission of the offence.

issues.issue: Can the delegate's decision to refer the report for an admissibility hearing stand?
issues.applicant_position: The referral rested on an untenable reading of s. 36(1)(a), so it cannot stand.
issues.respondent_position: Referral was a reasonable interpretation within the range defensible on the law.
issues.result_quote: Because that opinion was premised on an untenable interpretation of the grounds for inadmissibility under s. 36(1)(a), his decision to refer the Report cannot be sustained.
